subject: journey/che-guevara
prompt:
Use case: historical-scene. Asset type: journey sketchbook card.
An illustrated page from an explorer's journal: one particular moment on the journey, drawn close enough to see faces, hands, tools, clothing and the things being traded, measured or found. The traveller need not appear: some pages record only what the party saw (a harbour, a fortress, a market, an animal or plant). When the traveller does appear, draw them in action and in a natural, varied pose, not standing to attention. In the manner of the expedition artists of the 18th and 19th centuries. A visible graphite underdrawing with construction lines left in; quick sepia and brown ink with loose hatching; watercolour dropped in quickly and unevenly in a few washes of ochre, grey-green, faded blue and a touch of red. The page may carry one or two small separate studies of a detail (an object, a tool, a creature) loosely arranged beside the main scene, as on a real sketchbook page. Edges unfinished, dissolving into bare, slightly foxed cream paper; a single page, no binding visible. No legible writing of any kind: no annotations, labels, captions, numbers, dates or signature; any writing that appears in the scene is illegible marks. No border or frame. Nothing anachronistic for the year given; people, dress and objects true to their place and time, drawn with respect.
One coherent landscape 3:2 composition. Place and date: Machu Picchu, 1952.
Ernesto Guevara in 1952, age 23 to 24, slim young Argentine man with short dark wavy hair and clean-shaven face or light travel stubble, worn civilian shirt and trousers; Alberto Granado age 29, stockier with receding dark hair, civilian shirt and trousers. No iconic later Che beret, military uniform, star, cigar, weapons or revolutionary posters. Include travelers only when the scene requests them, never an obligatory foreground figure.
Scene: Wide accurate classic elevated view of Machu Picchu with Huayna Picchu behind, 1952 sparse visitors absent, roofless granite buildings and terraces following ridge contours, deep forested valley, cloud. No giant fantasy temples or reconstructed thatched roofs everywhere.
Believable geometry and anatomy. Do not add a motorcycle to scenes after its breakdown. No readable text, watermark or signature.
edits: Edit this page to show ONLY the grand Machu Picchu landscape. Remove both foreground people, all their belongings and all separate inset drawings. Restore the terraces, grass and stone buildings where the people stood. Widen the main continuous view across the ridge, with Huayna Picchu and forested valley behind. Preserve realistic Inca site geometry and sepia graphite watercolor style. No people, portraits, labels, writing or modern tourist facilities anywhere. Landscape fills the page.
